sentences.text: Researchers administered hesperidin, a flavonoid, orally to 100 C57BL/6 mice for 21 days following spinal cord injury, dividing them into sham, injury-only, and three dose groups.
By day 21, only the highest dose group demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in motor and sensory function, whereas lower doses did not reach statistical significance.

Tissue analysis on day 7 revealed that the high-dose group had lower levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokine TNF-α and the oxidative stress marker MDA, alongside higher activities of antioxidant enzymes SOD, GSH-Px, and CAT.
This treatment was also associated with fewer activated microglia cells and reduced phosphorylation of the signaling proteins ERK1/2 and JNK, while total protein amounts remained unchanged.
The authors conclude that further experiments are needed to prove that hesperidin directly causes these improvements, rather than just being associated with them.
